beats.text: A backend for apps that AI agents use. Six steps, one minute.
One command. Docker is the only thing you need.
It writes the secrets and builds the images on your machine.
It prints the panel URL and a one-time setup token. Keep both.
Describe the data once: its fields and who may read or write it.
The access rule is required. No rule means no.
From that one file: REST, MCP tools, an admin form and a typed SDK.
In the panel: Agents, New agent. Give it a name.
Pick only the scopes it needs. Admin stays off.
It gets its own key. Not the database password.
Point Claude Code, Cursor or Codex at the MCP server.
The key comes from the environment, never from a file in git.
The agent only sees the tools its scopes allow.
A read passes every check and returns only its own rows.
Reaching too far gets a 403 with a code and a hint.
Both land in the audit log, per agent.
With approvals on, a delete does not run. It becomes a proposal.
It waits in your inbox, with what would change.
You approve. It runs once, and the audit log says who decided.
Open source, MIT licensed. Install it in one command.
